issue_context.title: Clearer error message for unfound extensions
issue_context.body:
When trying to install an extension that isn't found (possibly because of being logged into an Enterprise host as in #6393 or because of a typo) the error `extension is not installable: missing executable`. This makes it sound like the extension was found, but cannot be installed.

In this situation, a more clear error should be shown, like:

```
X Could not find extension 'github/gh-gei' on host ghe.foo.bar 
```

This will hopefully help people figure out what's going on; if not, it'll help us diagnose issues more quickly.
comments: This seems like a duplicate of https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/5148 but this issue has more details so I will close the old one.

review_comments:
I don't love that this returns a boolean and an error for such a short function. I'm wondering if it should only return an error or nil, but it feels strange to return an error for the lack of existence of a repo 🤔 

at the same time, due to the http call I do need to return an error

I don't think that it feels odd to return both a boolean and an error. One thing we can do is just return an error and have a nice error message for a 404 response indicating that the repo does not exist. We do something similar in `HasMinimumScopes` in `oauth_scopes.go`.
Looks like we have explicit return parameters now, can we remove the named return parameters to reduce confusion going forward?
